one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-14 to 2026-11-13. Scheduled: Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-04 (Quartr calendar via Bigdata.com), the first quarter with SkyWater (2 months) consolidated; FY2026 guide is $450-460M. IonQ beat its revenue guidance in recent quarters (Q2 revenue 20% above the guidance midpoint), and Polymarket's GAAP-EPS 'beat' markets resolved Yes for Q4-25 and Q1-26 and No for Q2-26, when the warrant mark-to-market caused the miss. GAAP EPS will again be swamped by warrant fair-value swings, so the reaction should hinge on revenue, RPO and combined 2027 commentary. Also in the window: settlement of the $2.0B unit offering ($40 per share + 2 Series C warrants at $69.46; directors' lock-up 30 days; company 60 days), and possible Elisity close (guided Q4; at prices below the $33.07 collar floor IonQ issues the maximum ~34.8M shares). The stock fell ~9% today and ~21% over 5 days, with QNT -19% over 5 days. That is a sector-wide derating plus the offering's value transfer (the 2 warrants per $40 unit are worth roughly $3/share of existing value on my Black-Scholes), so short-horizon reversal and continued negative sector momentum roughly offset. Stocktwits retail sentiment turned bearish on the Elisity deal. I centre the 1-month distribution at $31.0 (slightly below spot for the Elisity issuance overhang) with a monthly log-sd of 0.26 (92%/3.5) and no extra skew; earnings can move the stock about 10-15% either way.

fair_value.method: Blend of five creative methods (no multiple carries weight): milestone rNPV in a SOTP frame $17.08 (30%), TAM-share scenarios $16.79 (25%), cash floor + computing real option $16.79 (15%), transaction marks vs Quantinuum $22.55 (20%), consensus-path DCF $16.98 (10%). All on 513.55M horizon shares (incl. the 2026-10-14 $2.0B offering, Elisity at the collar floor and 12 months of SBC), $3.46B horizon net cash, and a deduction for the 179M Series A/B/C warrants. Value at horizon = $18.05.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: No multiple is used in the fair value (weight 0). thesis_break_reason: At $12 the market cap (~$6.2B on 514M horizon shares) would sit below net cash at horizon ($3.46B) plus SkyWater ($1.54B), Elisity ($0.89B) and the acquired networking/space/sensing units at haircut cost ($1.31B), i.e. it would value the computing roadmap below zero. That would most likely mean a fundamental break (burn far above consensus, write-downs of acquired units, failed Superion/Stage C verification, or a much larger dilutive raise) rather than normal volatility. My fair value ($18) is already below spot, so the break is placed under the operating-unit floor, not under spot.

reverse_dcf_check: Today's price ($31.545) on 513.55M horizon shares plus ~$1.9B of warrant value, less net cash ($3.46B), SkyWater, Elisity and the non-computing units, leaves ~$10.9B for the computing platform at the horizon, versus my probability-weighted $2.1-2.2B. Put another way, the FMP consensus path extended to 2035 (revenue $4.65B in 2035, EBITDA margin 35%, SBC costed) is worth only $5.9B for all operations at 16% and supports today's price only at a 3.6% discount rate. At 16% the price needs roughly 2.5x those 2035 cash flows (2035 revenue around $11-12B at the same margins), i.e. near-certain leadership (my leader state, 15.5% likely). The engine's multiples carry zero weight, so its implied WACC is not informative here. The gap is why my fair value is $18: the market prices the leader state as near-certain, while independent signals (Manifold: 1,000 logical qubits by 2028 only 15%; Superion 256 deliveries already pushed to 2027) do not support that.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $312.0M (F43); TTM $450.0M (F46). Up to the horizon SBC is counted as dilution (+16M shares on a ~$500M run-rate including Elisity's $100M RSUs); after the horizon it is costed in GAAP EBIT margins in the rNPV/TAM states and in the consensus-path DCF. Each period is counted once. Consensus EBITDA (adjusted) is used only after subtracting SBC.

reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $80.1M (+287%), FY26 guide $450-460M incl. SkyWater (closed 7/31 for $1.8B: 24.1M shares + $741M cash), TTM GAAP operating loss -$1.0B, SBC $450M TTM. Today (10/14) IonQ launched a $2.0B unit offering at $40 (1 share + 2 Series C warrants @ $69.46, 7-yr), on top of 79M Series A/B warrants, and on 10/12 agreed to buy Elisity for $1.15B in stock (collar $33.07-$49.61). Diluted horizon shares ~514M vs 381M at 6/30. Valuation: no multiple works (pure-play peers at 135-325x sales), so I value cash + operating units at marks + the computing roadmap as an option/probability tree. Computing is worth ~$2.1-2.2B (rNPV and TAM), $2.1B (real option), $5.5B (0.8x QNT's public EV); the market implies ~$10.9B. Fair value $18.05 (methods $16.8-$22.6). Alternative-lane evidence: DARPA QBI Stage C selection (QCR, PostQuantum, Hacker News lead) is the main positive. Roadmap slippage: PostQuantum reports first 256-qubit chips and ions trapped, deliveries in 2027. Manifold crowd odds: 1,000 logical qubits by 2028 only 15%; Q-Day before 2030 17.6%. Polymarket gives a US stake in IonQ 10% (event volume ~$215K, IonQ leg ~$5K). Hiring keeps rising (LinkUp active jobs 167 in Sep-26, +151% YoY; Greenhouse 131 roles), which means more burn. Developer pull is weak (qiskit-ionq PyPI downloads 110K in Apr-26 vs 53K in Sep-26). Stocktwits retail sentiment turned bearish on the Elisity deal. USAspending shows IonQ-group prime DoD contracts are small ($13.4M IonQ, $59.7M Vector Atomic, $13.0M Capella), so most government revenue must come through other vehicles (OTAs, subcontracts) or non-DoD agencies. Defense/intelligence share: the company says ~60% of Q2-26 revenue was commercial, meaning non-U.S.-government (CFO on the call), so ~40% came from U.S. government customers. The defense/intelligence split is not disclosed. After the close, SkyWater's ATS revenue ($212.5M of $442.1M in FY2025, tied largely to aerospace and defense) and DARPA QBI (up to $300M) likely raise the defense share. Distribution: fair value is well below spot, but stocks like this rarely converge within 12 months, and the sector is in a sharp drawdown that could reverse. So I put the median at ~$23-24 (partial convergence) with a wide mixture (bear $14 / base $25 / bull $52, within-scenario log-sd 0.45-0.48; overall ~0.67, below the 92% realized). P(>=today's price) ~33%. Lane ratio: 14 of 41 sources are alternative-lane; the rest are filings needed for share count, cash, warrants and deals. Reddit (403), Wikipedia pageviews (429), X and McKinsey's own page (503) could not be reached, Kerrisdale coverage was unverifiable (403) and was dropped, and the Twelve Data estimates needed a higher plan, so research was limited.

model_inputs.structure_note: A 5-year DCF cannot describe IonQ: GAAP EBIT is deeply negative through FY2030 even on consensus (EBIT before SBC still -$122M in FY2030), so the engine's DCF/Gordon leg is meaningless and gets weight 0; the multiple leg is a weight-0 sanity check. Value is carried by five custom legs (rNPV, TAM, real option, transaction marks, consensus-path DCF to 2035) that include the pending Elisity shares, the Oct-2026 offering and the warrant overhang.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the weighted custom legs ($18.05). Scenario deltas (custom_pct) carry the price scenarios: the base scenario ($25) sits above fair value because I expect only partial convergence within 12 months.
